reference: 0.1% for QRRE revolvers and 0.05% for other retail exposures; the PD used is the higher of the grade/pool PD and the floor. PD of defaulted retail exposures is 100%.

result.question: What PD input floors apply to retail exposures under CRR3?
result.answer:
Under Art. 163(1) CRR, the PD used as an input to the RWEA and expected loss formulae is the higher of the one-year PD of the internal grade or pool and the following floors [C2]:

- **0,1 %** for QRRE revolvers [C2]
- **0,05 %** for retail exposures that are not QRRE revolvers [C2]

The floors apply only for calculating risk-weighted exposure amounts and expected loss amounts [C2]. They do not apply to the part of an exposure covered by an eligible guarantee from a central government, central bank or the ECB. The uncovered part remains subject to the floors [C5].

claims.text: For retail exposures, the PD used as an input to the risk-weighted exposure amount and expected loss formulae is the higher of the one-year PD associated with the internal borrower grade or pool and the PD input floor.
The PD input floor is 0,1 % for QRRE revolvers.
The PD input floor is 0,05 % for retail exposures which are not QRRE revolvers.
The PD input floors apply for the sole purpose of calculating risk-weighted exposure amounts and expected loss amounts.

PD, LGD and CCF input floors do not apply to the part of an exposure covered by an eligible guarantee from a central government, central bank or the ECB, while the uncovered part remains subject to them.

context.title: Non-application of PD, LGD and CCF input floors
